neighbours.label: A feature being weighed as a tell-tale sign of something: fires in the slot just before or after an evidence word ('a defining symptom of', 'taken as further proof that', 'tell from the … whether'); its output promotes 'hallmark', 'signature', 'evidence', 'distinguishing'
fire: A persistent dry cough is not a defining symptom of the common cold, nor even a frequent one.
The worn teeth were taken as further proof that the animal had fed on tough grasses.
Dealers can usually tell from the glaze whether a vase is a genuine antique.
Jointed legs are actually a definitive characteristic of insects, so the specimen must be one.
Fever alone is not a distinguishing feature of malaria, since many infections cause it.
If the swelling goes down after the antihistamine, then this increases our confidence that it was an allergy.
The scratches on the bone were seen as additional evidence that the hunters used stone tools.
Unusual levels of iridium in the clay were regarded as further evidence that an asteroid had struck.
quiet: A persistent dry cough can be treated with honey and plenty of warm fluids.
The worn teeth were cleaned and stored in a drawer at the museum.
Dealers can usually sell a vase like this within a week of buying it.
Jointed legs allow insects to walk, jump and cling to smooth stems.
Fever alone can make a child tired, thirsty and unwilling to eat.
If the swelling goes down after lunch, we will walk to the shops together.
The scratches on the bone were made when the box was dropped by movers.
Unusual amounts of rain fell on the valley and flooded the lower fields.

notes: Card and look: diagnostic reasoning (defining symptom, further evidence, linguistic fingerprints, 'the handling indicates'). Probes: 'not a defining symptom of' 0.40, 'further proof that' 0.41, 'tell from the stitching whether' 0.24; but 'the brushwork suggests' 0.04 and 'strongly implies' 0.02, and diagnostic if-clauses only 0.12-0.34. So the wording of the evidence slot matters more than inference in general; one fire item (the if-clause) tests the weaker form.
